stories.title: Trading partners oppose proposed US tariffs as aircraft maker warns of higher costs
stories.summary: China, Brazil and other trading partners challenged Washington's November 25 tariff proposals on Thursday. China urged negotiations and reserved its right to respond. Brazilian aircraft manufacturer Embraer warned that proposed duties on its products could increase US airline costs. The package remained subject to consultation.

commonFacts.text: The November 25 proposal targets 14 trading partners and uses Section 301 of the 1974 Trade Act.
The package includes a proposed 10% duty on aircraft imported from Brazil.
The measures had not yet entered into effect and were subject to a further process.

framingDifferences.text: Disputed question: are the unilateral tariffs a justified remedy for foreign industrial distortions? Position A: US trade representative Jamieson Greer in tar26-a cites US investigations into excess capacity and subsidies as grounds for action. Position B: Chinese commerce spokesperson He Yadong and other trading partners in tar26-b reject the approach; Japan disputes the claimed domestic distortions and China favors negotiation. The evidence establishes the proposed measures and the competing official assessments, not the validity of every US finding.

The reports converge on the proposal. tar26-r provides a concrete counterargument from Embraer: US demand and sourcing mean the aircraft levy could burden American customers. This is a forecast, not an observed price change; AP also includes objections, and TIME reports the US justification.

uncertainties: Final duties, exemptions and consultation outcomes.
Whether existing trade agreements would be altered or retaliation imposed.
Actual effects on capacity, inflation, airline costs and supply chains.

stories.title: Bulgaria offers civilian-only participation in Ukraine loan as EU budget dispute deepens
stories.summary: At the Brussels summit, Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev signaled support for civilian assistance within the proposed €45 billion Ukraine loan, but excluded weapons financing. Germany maintained its demand for broad participation, while several governments resisted linking the loan to the next EU budget.
stories.whyItMatters: The financing could help sustain Ukraine's public services and defense, while the dispute affects the EU's ability to agree on long-term spending and collective security commitments.
stories.selectionRationale: A material change in a member government's position on a major cross-border war-financing proposal, amid negotiations over the EU's multiannual budget.
stories.evidenceNote: Euronews was published before the later Bulgarian announcement. Its earlier description of four holdouts is not treated as an opposing factual interpretation. The later Guardian and Reuters accounts corroborate Radev's conditional position. No subsequent summit outcome is assumed.

The proposal separates up to €25 billion for military support and up to €20 billion for nonmilitary support.
Radev said Bulgaria would participate in nonmilitary support but not weapons funding.

framingDifferences.text: Disputed question: should agreement on the EU budget be conditioned on universal participation in Ukraine financing? Position A: Merz in eu26-a argues that common European funding requires common responsibility. Position B: Fico in eu26-b rejects the linkage as coercive; some diplomats warn it may make compromise harder. These are attributed policy judgments. The reports establish the ultimatum and dissent, not which tactic will succeed.

The accounts converge on the funding dispute. eu26-r documents Bulgaria's conditional civilian-only commitment, showing a possible partial compromise. The earlier Euronews account predates this development; differing holdout counts do not constitute contradictory evidence.

uncertainties: Final participation and approval of the loan.

Timing and terms of any disbursements.

stories.title: Italy and Kuwait attribute fatal incident to Iran; Tehran denies involvement
stories.summary: Kuwaiti and Italian officials reported that two Italian civilian employees died after an incident at a facility in Kuwait. Kuwait attributed the attack to Iran, whose military and foreign minister denied involvement. Tehran offered a joint investigation, according to Reuters. Independent responsibility was not established in the selected coverage.
stories.whyItMatters: The deaths and conflicting accounts risk worsening relations between Iran, Gulf states and European governments during an already internationalized conflict.
stories.selectionRationale: A new fatal incident affecting nationals of a third country amid a conflict with substantial regional and international security consequences.
stories.evidenceNote: The AP original regional roundup and Anadolu original dispatch are independent of Reuters. Their reporting draws on government statements. The AP headline attributes the attack more categorically than its Kuwait section, which attributes the claim and includes Iran's denial. No independent forensic evidence was established.
